correctness.rationale: The exact root lattice and face fan are specified. The polar is a cube intersected with the integral slab. For even cycle length 2r its vertices are exactly balanced cube corners, in number choose(2r,r). Each facet cone has 2r primitive rays with the single full-support balanced ±1 relation, and every 2r−1 of them give an integral lattice basis, so only the maximal cones are singular. The dual affine semigroup consists of nonnegative vectors whose r plus coordinates and r minus coordinates have equal total. Pairing gives r² generators and swaps of partners give exactly the 2×2 minors. It follows that every singular chart is the rank-one r×r cone. Its Segre degree yields multiplicity choose(2r−2,r−1), its regular stratum and Picard quotient yield isolated support and class group ℤ, and the balanced semigroup is normal Gorenstein and Cohen–Macaulay. The finite checker n=3,…,10 verifies examples only, not the infinite reasoning.

originality.rationale: The exact object has appeared in three directly inspected sources. Matsui et al. introduced the symmetric-edge polytope and considered its Ehrhart geometry; Higashitani proved the smoothness parity criterion for symmetric directed graphs; Ohsugi–Shibata v1 worked out Gröbner bases and Ehrhart polynomials. Neither their general global criterion nor their projective-polytope toric ideal determines the local semigroup ring of the Fano face-fan toric variety, the binomial singular-point count as toric fixed points, or the rank-one r-by-r analytic chart with its multiplicity. The odd-cycle smoothness and even-cycle nonsmoothness statements are explicitly removed from the originality claim. Targeted equivalent-formulation comparisons found no same or stronger local classification in reviewed sources or indexed related findings. Unindexed equivalent results remain possible.
residual_risks: An unpublished, unindexed, or differently worded toric-Fano classification could have worked out the same local rank-one cones.

value.rationale: For a basic infinite family of symmetric-edge reflexive Fano polytopes, the literature identifies smoothness parity but not the full geometry of the nonsmooth members. Determining all singular orbit closures as precisely choose(2r,r) isolated points, their exact determinantal local rings, and the rapidly growing multiplicities is a natural complete singularity classification. It clarifies what the elementary graph-theoretic even-cycle obstruction actually produces geometrically; it is not an arbitrary finite invariant or mere reformulation of nonsmoothness. The result does not assert a general-graph classification, and the prior parity criterion is credited.
